experiment: J7 closure — capture determinism and inference determinism, measured apart
question: does an unchanging page yield a bit-identical captured frame on every fresh stream, and is the detector bit-exact on a fixed frame?
invocationMethod: a person clicked the extension's toolbar action once; nothing in this process produced, simulated or substituted for the click
notAJ7Run: one image, one device scale, no RE-1 scoring and no gate verdict; this does not re-run J7 and does not alter G1-G4

frozen.detectorHost: createTr01Host — the same factory the product wires at apps/extension/host/offscreen/main.ts:101, differing only in the instrumented worker spawn seam

phaseA.measures: capture determinism: does an unchanging page yield a bit-identical frame on every fresh stream?

phaseB.measures: inference determinism on a genuinely fixed input — the EXACT RGBA a real stream capture produced

phaseC.measures: inference determinism on the frozen held-out PNG — criterion 6's 'two consecutive runs on the same fixture', literally; a cross-check on Phase B, not a substitute
phaseC.note: the PNG is read in Node, which is the established pattern in run-tr01-worker.mjs; no STREAM frame crosses the boundary, so serviceWorkerSawNoPixels is untouched

liveVsFixture.note: MEASURED, not a G-3 verdict: this compares detector output on one image at one device scale, not the two pixel sources. G-3 remains open.

notAClaim: one image, one device scale, one window, one operator, one run. A bit-stable capture here does not prove the capture is bit-stable in general, and a non-zero variation rate here is this run's rate, not a population rate.
the earlier G4 failures (W1 DPR 1.25/H4 and 1.5/H3; W2 run 1 DPR 1.0/H1) were recorded without frame digests, so nothing measured here can be applied to them as FACT.
